labels.label: sbierski:lem:3.3

hypotheses.note: abstract setting: a continuous T strictly increasing along <=_M is CARRIED (M Hausdorff); in the abstract framework GH(M) does not give T and T does not give GH, so the two are incomparable and T is an added hypothesis. Compact diamonds are never used. T is automatic for smooth GH spacetimes, and is derived from GH only under theo:geroch's (i)=>(ii) hypotheses (injective_of_globallyHyperbolic, via geroch_i_imp_ii). sbierski_lemma_3_3 carries GH(M) AND T.

principal form (injOn_of_injOn_cauchy, injective_of_injOn_cauchy): only N Hausdorff and causal (weaker than GH). injective_of_mapsTo_cauchy carries CausallyArcConnected and CurvesExtend of N; sbierski_lemma_3_3 carries GH(N) (its conclusion IsCauchyEmbedding contains it) AND CausallyArcConnected and CurvesExtend of N, as model facts (kb/0012) — strictly more than Sbierski prints in the abstract setting, automatic for smooth spacetimes.

hypotheses.paper: Sigma' a Cauchy surface of M'
hypotheses.note: only phi(Sigma) acausal in N; injective_of_mapsTo_cauchy recovers Sbierski's form (phi(Sigma) inside a Cauchy surface Sigma', acausal by IsCauchySurface.isAcausal)
abstract E-morphism IsEMorphismOn / IsEMorphism (DEC-17); shown to be a local homeomorphism (exists_chart_of_isEMorphismOn)
injective on Sigma; surjectivity onto Sigma' used only for the IsCauchyEmbedding conclusion
Sigma a Cauchy surface of an open U of M (IsCauchySurfaceOn U), conclusion InjOn phi U, kb/0001; T strict along <=_M on all of M
not used: only uniqueness of lifts along a local homeomorphism with Hausdorff source

findings: Sbierski 1309.7591 Lemma 3.3 (p.13, pdftotext l.611-613): of 'psi|Sigma a diffeomorphism onto Sigma' only injectivity on Sigma and acausality of psi(Sigma) are used; neither GH of M' nor the Cauchy property of Sigma' is needed for injectivity.

Sbierski's step 'the geodesics psi.gamma and psi.sigma cannot intersect Sigma' more than once' is the acausality of psi(Sigma) together with causality of M'; his inextendible geodesic sigma is the maximal lift of psi.gamma, inextensible because it has no limit at its end (exists_lift), completed by an inextensible T-parametrised curve kappa (exists_inextensible_of_timeFunction).

labels.label: prop:Cauchy_pgcd

hypotheses.paper: phi : pgcd -> M2 a M>=0-morphism with phi.i1 = i2
hypotheses.note: instantiate U = pgcd (open of M1), Sigma = i1(Sigma0); phi injective on Sigma since i2 is. The instantiation ALSO needs two things beyond the paper's hypotheses: (a) a continuous T on M1 strictly increasing along <=_{M1} (a time function of M1; in the abstract setting not given by GH(M1), cf. theo:geroch (i)=>(ii)), and (b) acausality of phi(Sigma) = i2(Sigma0) in M2, which in the abstract setting comes from IsCauchySurface.isAcausal and needs CausallyArcConnected and CurvesExtend of M2 (model facts, kb/0012). Both are automatic for smooth spacetimes.

findings: ETT.tex:1945-1966: the proof never shows phi : pgcd -> M2 injective, so (pgcd, phi) is not shown to be a common sub-extension (ETT ledger gap 1, SubExtension 'nothing shows phi injective'). injOn_of_injOn_cauchy closes this gap in the open-set form the union needs; assembling cauchy_pgcd is package Pgcd.

labels.label: theo:CBG
findings: Design §3 step 2 (Sbierski Lemma 3.3) supplied: morphisms of Cauchy developments (f.phi = phi') are injective, hence Cauchy embeddings, without being asked to be.

kb_proposals: Path lifting along a local homeomorphism with Hausdorff source is in CBG/Injective.lean (exists_lift: full segment or half-open [a,e) with no limit; IsLiftOn.eqOn uniqueness): reuse it for any curve-lifting argument instead of geodesics.
An IsEMorphismOn C D U phi is a local homeomorphism on U with charts sourced in U (exists_chart_of_isEMorphismOn) and is a morphism of the dual causalities (isEMorphismOn_dual).
In the abstract framework GH(M) does not give a time function; theorems needing one carry T (continuous, strict along <=_M) and get it from geroch_i_imp_ii only under theo:geroch's hypotheses.
